raw_case_text:
A 25 year old woman was referred with a history of chronic headache for a period of three months. The headache was severe and refractory to NSAIDs or other pain relievers. There was no history of chills and fever, gait disturbance, hearing loss and memory problems. No history of using illicit drugs such as cocaine, alcohol, cannabis was also found. Drug history was negative for oral contraceptive pills, nalidoxic acid, tetracycline, corticosteroids, vitamin A and other drugs. She was student, lived in an urban area with history of travels to rural areas. No history of using unpasteurized milk and contact with animals were found. 
 In physical examination, vital signs were normal. Generally, she was cooperative with intact orientation. Cranial nerve examinations were normal and meningeal signs were not detected. There was a significant papilledema in ophthalmologic examination. Deep tendon reflexes (DTRs) in upper and lower limbs were normal. Muscle forces in proximal and distal regions of lower and upper limbs were also normal. No impairment in the sensation of extremities was detected. Gait was intact with no ataxia and tremor. Psychological examination was also done. There was not any abnormality in mood and affect evaluation and no cognitive impairment was also observed. 
 Laboratory studies including complete blood count with differentiation (CBC/ diff), prothrombin time (PT), partial thromboplastin time (PTT), international normalized ratio (INR), blood urea nitrogen, creatinine (BUN,Cr) and liver function tests (LFT) were normal. An elevated ESR was detected (68mm/hour). HBS Ag, HCV Ab, VDRL and HIV Ab were also negative. Anti-nuclear antibody (ANA), Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), C3 and C4 were in normal range. Brain CT scan in addition to T1 and T2 weighted brain MRI plains after gadolinium injections were also performed that revealed no pathologic findings. The patient underwent lumbar puncture. Cerebrospinal fluid appeared xanthochromic and presented with a high opening pressure (280 mmH2O), low glucose (43mg/dl) and elevated protein levels (338mg/dl). Spinal fluid analysis showed leukocytes. Brucella (capt test) tube agglutinin was positive at 1/2560 titers in blood and positive at spot and 1/2560 titers in CSF. Tuberculosis PCR test was negative for the CSF sample. 
 In summary, we had a case with a history of chronic headache characterized by increased intra-cranial pressure (ICP). Papilledema was the only positive finding in the initial physical examination. SAT (serum antibody test) was the only positive finding for brucella within the laboratory test. Other investigations including imaging studies were normal. The patient received intravenous cefteriaxone 1gr BID and oral doxycycline 100mg BID and rifampin 600 mg once daily for 1 month; and then rifampin continued for 14 months. Headache began to improve during treatment and disappeared after 3 months.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 25-year-old female presented with a 3-month history of severe, chronic headache refractory to analgesics.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed severe, unremitting headache over a 3-month period that was refractory to NSAIDs and other pain relievers. She had no fever, chills, gait disturbance, hearing loss, or memory problems. She sought specialized neurological evaluation where bilateral papilledema was detected.
subjective.past_medical_history: Student residing in an urban area with a history of travel to rural areas. Denied consuming unpasteurized milk or contact with animals. Negative history for illicit drug use (cocaine, cannabis, alcohol). Medication history negative for oral contraceptive pills, nalidixic acid, tetracyclines, corticosteroids, and vitamin A.
subjective.review_of_systems: Severe chronic headache. Denied fever, chills, gait instability, hearing loss, memory deficits, mood disturbances, or cognitive impairment. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: normal. Neurological: alert, oriented, and cooperative; cranial nerves intact; meningeal signs absent; motor examination normal with 5/5 muscle strength in upper and lower extremities; deep tendon reflexes (DTRs) normal; sensory examination intact; gait normal without ataxia or tremor; psychological evaluation revealed normal mood, affect, and intact cognition. Ophthalmologic: significant bilateral papilledema.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC with differential, PT, PTT, INR, BUN, creatinine, and liver function tests: all normal. ESR: elevated at 68 mm/hour. Serologies: HBsAg, HCV Ab, VDRL, and HIV Ab were negative. Autoimmune panel: ANA, ANCA, C3, and C4 within normal limits.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain CT scan: normal. Brain MRI (T1- and T2-weighted plain and gadolinium-enhanced images): normal, no pathologic findings. Lumbar puncture: CSF xanthochromic with elevated opening pressure of 280 mmH2O, low glucose of 43 mg/dL, elevated protein of 338 mg/dL, and presence of leukocytes. CSF PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis: negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Neurobrucellosis presenting with intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri-like syndrome) and bilateral papilledema.
Confirmation: Brucella Coombs (Capt test) tube agglutination test positive at 1/2560 titer in blood, and positive at spot and 1/2560 titer in CSF.
Differentials ruled out: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension secondary to medications, intracranial mass lesion, cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, viral/syphilitic/HIV central nervous system infections, tuberculous meningitis (negative CSF PCR), and systemic vasculitis/autoimmune diseases (normal ANA, ANCA, C3, C4).
Treatment & Outcome: Treated with intravenous ceftriaxone (1 g BID), oral doxycycline (100 mg BID), and oral rifampin (600 mg once daily) for 1 month, followed by rifampin continuation for 14 months. Headache improved during therapy and completely resolved after 3 months.
